title.narrative: Land for Peace: Qualified and increased workforce to enhance land administration processes to support peacebuilding and rural economic development

description.narrative:
Impact, outcomes and outputs The project has to contribute to the following impact and must achieve the outcomes and outputs as stated below.
Long-term impact: Social and economic reconstruction: income generating and livelihoods opportunities to prevent the (re)occurrence of conflicts, instability or irregular migration.
Medium-term impact that will contribute to this: (I) Education system (TVET/HE) is of good quality, relevant and accessible (SDG 4); (II) Partnerships between persons and organisations are inclusive and sustainable (SDG 17); (III) Organisations key to (sectoral) inclusive development of partner countries are strengthened by inflow of enhanced workforce.
Outcomes of the project: A. TVET/HE organisations (in the selected partner countries and in NL) perform better their core tasks, firmly embedded in their environment (in line with country / regional specific labour market needs & aiming at inclusiveness).
To that end, the following outputs must be achieved by the end of the project:
1. Revised and updated curricula on the level of of BSc, Diploma and developed Certificate (ToT) in Land Administration (LA) and Surveying. 2. Qualified staff to develop and offer the revised and developed study programmes and to support research and outreach programmes. 3. The Faculty of Engineering and the Faculty of Environment and Natural Resources strengthened.

comment.narrative: 15-07-2020: Together with stakeholders involved, the project is contributing to programme improvements (demand driven) in the first year. Only in the second reporting period, actual changes will be proposed and then incorporated into the programme. Any modifications still need to go through an approval process by the accreditation committee.
1 BSc and 1 Diploma course; 1 ToT course developed

title.narrative: A.O.11. Number of organisations with policies and procedures to ensure an environment which is gender sensitive

comment.narrative: 15-07-2020: As indicated, UD has a particular interest in addressing students from marginalised groups and always promotes a proper gender balance for staff and students. However, for being technical Faculties, this still remains a challenge.
UD has an institutional policy on Social Inclusion. Gender might be part of this policy

title.narrative: A.O.6. Number of facilities established/strengthened

comment.narrative: 15-07-2020: Both, the Faculty of Engineering and the Faculty of Environment and Natural Resources of UD were strengthened during the first reporting period through their participation on key activities of the project.
18-02-2022: There are separate facilities within each faculty for each of the two programs.

title.narrative: A.E.3. Number of staff that have gained qualitative and relevant knowledge and skills to develop and offer the revised/developed study programmes

comment.narrative: 15-07-2020: During the first reporting period, 12 of the 47 UD staff members involved in the project have gained qualitative and relevant knowledge to offer the (future) revised/developed study programmes.

title.narrative: A.E.1. Number of (knowledge) institutions supported directly

comment.narrative: 15-07-2020: During the first reporting period, Universidad Distrital Francisco José de Caldas (UD) was supported directly by the project partners through group discussions and workshops. Likewise, the OKP-UD working group met 31 times, to monitor the activities of the schedule and present partial results. All this information is available in the minutes of the meetings.

title.narrative: A.E.4. Number of graduates delivered

comment.narrative: 15-07-2020: Graduates of the improved programme are not delivered in the first reporting period. Together with stakeholders involved, the programme is currently being improved and becoming more demand driven based on the findings of a labor market analysis and an alumni survey.

title.narrative: A.S.5. Number of improvements in (inter)national policies/laws

comment.narrative: 15-07-2020: In the last year in Colombia, several public policies have been generated within the framework of the 'Multi-purpose Cadaster', which directly influences the curriculum, so a detailed study was carried out depicting the new rules and laws that must be taken into account in the revised curriculum.
18-02-2022: See mid-term evaluation report for details.

title.narrative: A.R.3. Number of relevant innovations

comment.narrative: 15-07-2020: Not yet achieved.

18-02-2022: although the new curricula are still under development, teacher already started to modify their educational approach to incorporate new tools and teaching methods in their educational activities.
State of the art methodologies in LA Incorporated in Research generated by the faculties through research seminars

title.narrative: A.O.2. Number of organisations revised/developed and implemented a strategic plan

comment.narrative: 15-07-2020: Not yet achieved.
UD Faculty of Engineering and the Faculty of Environment and Natural Resources strengthened

title.narrative: A.S.4. Number of SMEs supported

comment.narrative: 15-07-2020: Opportunities for self-employment and entrepreneurship will be explored, embedded as an option in the revised curricula (modules on employability and entrepreneurship) and facilitated by UD. Particularly in the field of community development and training, introduction of technological innovations in LA and services to training providers, we foresee opportunities for graduates to establish SME’s.

title.narrative: A.O.7. % of women in management of faculty/department

comment.narrative: 15-07-2020: The Faculty of Engineering currently has 25 administrative units, 8 of them are led by female staff members.

title.narrative: A.O.8. % of women of teaching staff of faculty/department

comment.narrative: 15-07-2020: The Faculty of Engineering has 164 teaching staff in total, 29 of them are female.

title.narrative: A.R.2. Number of relevant publications (level, gender, inclusion)

comment.narrative: 15-07-2020: This outcome will be achieved in the final year of the project. UD staff has submitted a number of articles in international seminars, for example, to the FIG working week in Amsterdam in May 2020. Unfortunately, due to the current crisis all such events have been cancelled or postponed. The teams of UD and ITC continue to work together in this front and more publication options, under the current restrictions, are being explored.
1 Peer review article published; 4 General publications

title.narrative: A.E.6. Number of students enrolled in revised/newly developed study programmes

comment.narrative: 15-07-2020: This outcome will only be achieved after the programme has been revised.
300 BSc graduates; 190 Diploma graduates; 200 ToT trainers trained; 45% female; 25% minorities

title.narrative: A.S.3. Number of students performing an internship or practical work

comment.narrative: 15-07-2020: This outcome will only be achieved after the study programme has been revised. The project is in close contact with the labour market. A gathering was organized in November 2019 to identify cooperation options between agencies and the UD. A number of proposals were formulated and will be acted upon in the following years.
internship opportunities created

title.narrative: A.S.2. Number of MoUs or other types of collaboration agreements signed (education, private, public, surrounding community)

comment.narrative: 15-07-2020: UD and the University of Twente/ITC signed a MoU for the purpose of this project. UD and the University of Applied Sciences and Arts Northwestern Switzerland School of Architecture, Civil Engineering and Geomatics (N/W) signed a MoU to carry out courses and transfer of knowledge.
4 MoUs between UD and consortium partners; 1 employer's advisory committee established

title.narrative: A.S.1. Number of beneficiaries in the society reached with knowledge, skills and techniques

comment.narrative: 18-02-2022: Seminars directed to Land Administration stakeholders.

24-09-2020: As a direct result of the some activities of the project, for example, the labor market study, professional organization are more aware of what the UD has to offer and in the year 2019, the UD carried out a number of training sessions and workshops to bring employees of those professional organizations up-to-date in some land administration areas. One such example id the National Mapping Agency who received training on RTX (real-time GNSS positioning), one of the latest GPS surveying techniques available today.
grass root surveyors trained
